I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I am 65, and I do not want to gamble on crops that need more labor, more market chasing, or more technical management. In Quzhou County, wheat and summer maize fit my land, water conditions, machinery, and my own experience. Wheat gives me a steady grain crop through the first half of the year, and maize follows right after harvest, so the land does not sit idle. I will use improved seed instead of old saved seed because I want more even emergence and steadier yield, but I will not choose management that is too complicated. I will plough before wheat where I need to break compaction, then use rotary tillage for maize after wheat harvest because time is tight. I will apply fertilizer at moderate levels, not too heavy, because I want yield but I also want to control cost. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, since wheat in my area depends more on timely water. For pests and disease, I will spray only as needed at the common key stages, because routine overuse wastes money. My goal is not the highest possible yield on paper. My goal is stable production, manageable work, and low risk.
